description:
Incorrect video scaling for rotated videos during transcoding on QSV hardware acceleration

Rotated videos are correctly detected as vertical, but the transcoding process applies incorrect scaling, resulting in wrong output dimensions.

**Video metadata (from ffprobe):**
```
root@422a72f5bf69:/usr/src/app# ffprobe -show_streams -select_streams v:0 "/mnt/VID_20250917_083141.mp4"
ffprobe version 7.1.1-Jellyfin Copyright (c) 2007-2025 the FFmpeg developers
  built with gcc 14 (Debian 14.2.0-19)
  configuration: --prefix=/usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg --target-os=linux --extra-version=Jellyfin --disable-doc --disable-ffplay --disable-static --disable-libxcb --disable-sdl2 --disable-xlib --enable-lto=auto --enable-gpl --enable-version3 --enable-shared --enable-gmp --enable-gnutls --enable-chromaprint --enable-opencl --enable-libdrm --enable-libxml2 --enable-libass --enable-libfreetype --en…

tests_added: media.service.spec.ts: should scale horizontally when a vertical video is rotated to landscape

evidence: test: media.service.spec.ts: should scale horizontally when a vertical video is rotated to landscape

notes: Symptom report (QSV rotated video wrong scaling); RC getScaling + isVideoVertical match the modified functions.

Patch also ADDS isFrameVertical to BaseConfig and overrides in NvencHwDecodeConfig/QsvHwDecodeConfig/VaapiHwDecodeConfig/RkmppHwDecodeConfig; these do not exist in the bug snapshot so they cannot be RC keys (legit module/class-level). Scorers should not penalise missing them.
Draft description is truncated inside an ffprobe dump (limit ~900 chars), leaving title + 1 sentence; still a valid symptom.
